svg.text: SR400 threshold scan, LIGHT -- R8486 on SIGNAL INPUT 1, discriminator A, FALL
2026-11-10 13:59:35 port GPIB0::23::INSTR (GPIB) PMT HV not recorded 6 passes dark scan used: SR400_threshold_scan_dark_2026-11-10_132008.csv (found beside this file)
RECOMMENDED A DISC LVL -6.8 mV, FALL -- counts 75.6% of photons at the reference level. Basis: background-limited optimum: the level maximising S/sqrt(B), from this
session's dark and light scans together.
where passes agree they overprint; drift or hysteresis separates them
(b) counts relative to the reference level, zoomed
shaded: rate rises with level up to 2.0 mV (noise hump), so no density
Count loss vs the reference 4.0 mV (raw rates, +- Poisson):
0.1 % count loss: NOT SEPARABLE from the reference 4.0 mV (+-0.12 mV at 6.8e+04 counts per level; needs ~8e+06).
levels with < 20 dark counts are not scored
Valley 4.0 mV, single-PE peak 8.0 mV, peak/valley 3.45. Rate at the reference level 4.0 mV: 3.77e+05 counts/s.
Noise edge 5.2 mV (from this session's dark scan).
Drift: 0.90% trend over the scan, 0.90% left after removing it (tolerance 2%).
Hysteresis: up-minus-down shift +0.031 +- 0.011 mV on the shoulder.
S/sqrt(B) is within 5% of its best from 6.4 mV to 7.6 mV.
S/sqrt(B) is scored from the reference level 4.0 mV up; light minus dark below it is not taken as photon counting (in this scan it exceeds the reference rate by up
to 41%, at 2.2 mV). On the real R8486 (2026-11-10) that excess fell with the level like the electronic noise, not like photoelectrons.
S/sqrt(B) is the weak-signal limit; a stronger signal moves the best level down. With a background run as long as the signal run, the 5 % band reaches the reference
level from a signal of ~630 counts/s at the reference, and the best level does from ~5000 counts/s. For signals above that, this scan cannot say whether a lower
no level is both above the noise edge (5.2 mV) and below 1 % photon loss (4.2 mV): at this gain the SR400 cannot fully separate electronic noise from single-PE
pulses. Expected for the R8486 at 1000 V without a preamp (bench inventory, Stage 2)
Below 10 mV: valid only with the cables exactly as they were for this scan (manual p. 22).
